parallel.requirements: The parent recognized ESM .mjs output, no external dependencies, no Uint8Array/DataView, manual CLI parsing, bech32 behavior from the executable, and exact stdout/exit behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It explored behavior first, then split implementation across four child agents: conversion constants, core checksum/string layer, segwit API, and CLI/entry assembly; the parent retained integration and final verification.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote separate modules under /output/lib. The segwit child implemented the parent-provided raw 5-bit model, which the parent later found was wrong and replaced with internal convertbits-based encode/decode behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After AgentSwarm returned, the parent listed the tree, ran the entry point, compared against the executable, rewrote segwitAddr.mjs, and delivered a single /output/lib plus test16.mjs artifact tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran syntax checks, four provided sample comparisons, a 74-case randomized and edge comparison, and a grep-style compliance check for disallowed APIs and CommonJS exports.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect remained at closure; the only resolved defect was the child-produced segwit API mismatch before the parent rewrite.

serial.requirements: The serial agent worked from the same prompt and recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argument parsing, bech32 behavior, local modules only, and exact executable comparison.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent owned all stages: module layout, checksum and conversion code, segwit API, CLI parser, entry point, debugging, and final verification.
serial.implementation: It wrote a bech32 directory plus args helper and entry file, then iteratively corrected padding, internal segwit conversion, and the checksum constant based on sample mismatches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All code was written and revised by the same actor in /output; final artifacts included test16.mjs, bech32 modules, and lib/args.mjs.
serial.verification: It compared the four sample cases, retried after each fix, performed randomized stdout/status comparisons, and reran the four samples before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect remained at closure; earlier mismatches were ordinary local implementation mistakes corrected before final delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM, no dependency, CLI, and executable-matching constraints and delivered passing files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the shared prompt and delivered passing files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement was missing at final output; parallel temporarily lost the package-level segwit conversion requirement in a child brief, while serial corrected the same behavior locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one AgentSwarm call with four child owners plus parent integration ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and kept all implementation, debugging, and verification ownership in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained modular parallelism but introduced a delegation boundary for segwit semantics; serial avoided delegation boundaries at the cost of doing all work sequentially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel fixed interface names and file owners in the swarm prompt, but the segwit child brief asserted the wrong raw 5-bit package behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context transfer and revised its own segwit model after observing mismatched sample output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context difference is the parallel child receiving an incomplete/wrong task-behavior brief, while serial retained context in one actor and corrected without handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote modular lib files, then the parent rewrote segwitAddr.mjs to import convertbits and match the executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its own bech32 module set and iteratively rewrote segwit.mjs and checksum handling until sample comparisons matched.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on the same behavior, but parallel had to replace a child module after integration whereas serial made the corrections within a single local implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned through AgentSwarm and the parent inspected them before integrated testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; local edits and test results stayed in the main timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join and inspection step that exposed a child result problem; serial had no result lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate owned files in a shared /output tree; parent then integrated and overwrote the completed segwit file as a corrective takeover.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and rewrote files itself without cross-agent shared-state ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace was coordinated by file ownership and produced no collision, but final integration required parent replacement of one child-owned library file.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used child-local tests, then whole-program sample comparisons, 74 randomized and edge cases, import/compliance checks, and passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used samples, random comparison, repeated final samples, and passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had sufficient final acceptance evidence; parallel's first integrated sample run exposed the child brief defect, then later verification closed the loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time, requests, tokens, and 49 tool calls, but completed within budget and closed only after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer resources and completed within budget after a shorter single-agent debugging loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred extra rework and coordination overhead but no budget failure; serial was more compact while reaching the same official outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official completed evaluations passed 26/26, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. Parallel reached the pass after child delegation, an incorrect segwit child brief, integrated sample failures, and parent takeover; serial reached the pass through a single-agent write/debug loop that corrected analogous ordinary implementation mistakes locally.
parallel_contributors: AgentSwarm produced most module implementations concurrently.
The segwit child brief omitted the correct internal conversion behavior and caused integrated sample failures before parent correction.
Parent final verification after rewriting segwitAddr.mjs closed the loop and produced a passing artifact.
serial_contributors: One actor retained the full task context and owned every module and correction.
Serial testing identified mismatched address behavior and led to local segwit and checksum fixes before delivery.
Final random and sample comparisons confirmed the single-agent artifact.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts initially misunderstood parts of the bech32 package behavior; in serial this stayed an ordinary local implementation defect, while in parallel one part was exported into a child brief.
Parallel used /output/lib module names while serial used /output/bech32 plus /output/lib/args.mjs; both structures satisfied the prompt and official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process episode rather than a failure cause

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned concrete implementation owners for every needed module through the four child scopes and the parent retained final integration authority.
The parent explicitly performed integration after AgentSwarm returned, ran sample comparisons, and rewrote the incompatible segwit module.
The final entry point and library tree were assigned and present, and artifact validation found the expected test16.mjs file.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from exploration to delegation, join, integrated testing, correction, and final response.
The parent did exploratory probing before delegation, but it was not a mandatory serial gate that left implementation unfinished or insufficiently verified.
Investigation did not remain a separate all-investigation phase that displaced later implementation; child implementation followed and final verification completed.
The indispensable integration path was owned by the parent and executed after child return; no needed work was starved of capacity before closure.
The four-child fan-out increased elapsed time and token use but did not exhaust the run budget or prevent final integration and verification.
No child received a scope too broad to complete; the segwit child completed its narrow file, but the brief semantics were wrong.

The executed segwit child was told to implement raw 5-bit encode/decode without internal convertbits behavior even though the task required matching the Python executable; the child followed that brief and produced a module the parent later had to replace.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child-produced segwit module made all four integrated sample comparisons fail, forcing a parent takeover and rewrite before the final passing verification.
candidates.near_match_reason: A concrete file and export contract existed between the entry and segwit modules; the missing item was the correct task behavior to preserve, not the interface shape itself.

candidates.reason: The swarm prompt defined file paths and exports for each module; the segwit problem was a wrong task semantic in the brief rather than absent interface ownership.
There is no evidence that known information disappeared during transfer; the relevant segwit fact was wrong in the initial child brief itself.
The AgentSwarm result was large but the parent consumed it, discussed agent findings, and proceeded to integrated tests and corrective edits.
No child or parent acted on a handoff describing a superseded workspace or requirement state; the problematic segwit model was initial, not stale.
Agent 1 reported vector inconsistency, but the parent adjudicated the issue through executable comparison rather than leaving conflicting handoffs unresolved.
The parent did not declare whole-task completion on child returns alone; it performed integrated sample, fuzz, and compliance checks before final response.
There was no replacement child or retry lacking inherited state; the parent directly fixed the segwit module after diagnosing the mismatch.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: All four child agents completed and returned; there is no explicit cancellation or interruption of an active needed child.
A directly promotable complete candidate was not left unplaced before closure; the parent corrected the only known mismatch and finalized after tests.
The corrective segwit rewrite happened before the successful sample and fuzz verification, not after the relevant integrated checks.
The parent joined all child outputs through AgentSwarm, listed the resulting file tree, and tested the integrated implementation.
No verifier child produced a trapped finding; verification was run by the parent after child completion and returned directly in the main timeline.
When integrated testing exposed the segwit failure, the parent took over and rewrote the module rather than leaving the failed child scope unresolved.
Completed child results were available and the parent used them in the integrated tree; it also explicitly discussed the agent-1 warning before testing.
The parent did not wait to a timeout without inspecting progress; it resumed after child completion and actively ran integration checks.
Agents wrote different assigned files with fixed imports; there were no competing designs claiming the same behavior after parent reconciliation.
No two live child agents edited the same file; the later segwit rewrite was a parent correction after the child had completed.
The parent overwrote a completed child source file as an intentional takeover after integrated failure, not as a concurrent replacement of another active owner.
The directly submitted entry point was not overwritten by competing live ownership, and the parent correction targeted a library module.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree provenance.
Although children wrote into a shared /output tree, file ownership was separated and no unstable-state or provenance problem was observed.
No child-generated fixture, cache, temporary file, or auxiliary implementation was consumed by another actor as a stable reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The executed segwit child was briefed with an incorrect raw 5-bit package API model and no internal conversion requirement, then produced a module that failed integrated executable comparison until parent takeover.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The child-produced segwit module made all four integrated sample comparisons fail, forcing a parent takeover and rewrite before the final passing verification.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The cross-agent module interface was specified; the error was the missing task-specific package behavior inside the segwit child brief.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The segwit failure chain was retained only as Incomplete Child Brief; Missing Cross-Agent Contract, Source Overwrite, No Failure Takeover, and Merge after Verification were rejected as downstream or near-match descriptions of the same corrected episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the segwit child-brief episode met the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional labels were added for normal fan-out cost, successful joins, parent corrective overwrite, or final verification because those were either non-adverse or downstream of the retained brief episode.
